name: Amlach
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful scattered settlement in the Drautal valley with sunny slopes and views of the Lienzer Dolomiten.
beschreibung:
Overview

Amlach is located at an altitude of 689 meters in the sunny Lienz valley basin of East Tyrol, situated right on the right bank of the Drau River immediately south of the district capital, Lienz. With approximately 530 residents and spanning nearly 22.5 square kilometers, this peaceful municipality in the district of Lienz encompasses the main village and the scenic hamlet of Ulrichsbichl. To the south, the dramatic rock faces of the Lienz Dolomites, most notably the Spitzkofel massif, dominate the horizon. Benefiting from its immediate proximity to Lienz, direct access to the Drau Cycle Path, and nearby Lake Tristacher See, Amlach harmoniously balances tranquil village charm with exceptional outdoor adventures.

History

The village name has Slavic roots derived from the word Jamljani, meaning 'valley dwellers', attesting to early settlement. The earliest documented mention of the settlement dates to 1352 under the name 'nemlach', when estates were deeded to the civic hospital in Lienz. For centuries, agriculture shaped daily life, while powerful alpine streams powered early water mills and the historic Galitzen smithy. In 1885 and 1886, local visionaries developed the breathtaking Galitzenklamm gorge by constructing wooden walkways and bridges, opening this natural wonder to international visitors and establishing Amlach's early tourism tradition.

Getting There

Thanks to its proximity to Lienz, Amlach is easily reached: from Lienz railway station—a major hub on the Drau Valley line with frequent trains from Klagenfurt, Spittal, and South Tyrol—it is just two to three kilometers to Amlach. This short distance can be traveled by regional bus, by taxi, or on foot in roughly twenty minutes via the Drau bridge. By car from Salzburg or Innsbruck, motorists take the Felbertauern road B108 to Lienz and branch off via the B100. From Italy, drivers arrive via the Pustertal highway. Cyclists can pedal directly into the village along the Drau Cycle Path (R1).

Tips

The undisputed highlight is the Galitzenklamm water adventure park at the foot of the Dolomites, featuring thundering waterfalls, secure cliff walkways, an educational water trail, a historic stone ball mill, and several via ferratas ranging from family routes to the extreme Dopamin-Klettersteig. A short woodland walk leads to Lake Tristacher See, East Tyrol's only natural swimming lake. Cultural heritage sites include the Church of Saint Odilia in the center and Saint Ulrich's Chapel atop the forested Ulrichsbichl hill. Amlach also boasts an equestrian center and serves as a premier base for high-altitude hikes to the Karlsbader Hütte.
